summary: Made and shipped the channel's first full 3D long video, L-20261123-21 'How Does Starlink's Flat Dish Aim Without Moving?' (7:06, 60 directed beats on 9 places, three rated thumbnails, A picked).
why: state --format long: 0 of 2 long videos this week; Scout's top usable topic (2026-11-18-starlink-flat-dish, priority high, 4.6M-view demand video).

findings.title: Fact review caught a stale feed figure
findings.detail: Starlink's 550 km altitude is out of date: SpaceX is lowering its satellites to about 480 km during 2026 (Space.com). The video uses 480 km; longform/topics.json corrected; research/topics.json still has 550 km (research's lane).

findings.title: Fact review round 3 caught a causal-order error
findings.detail: The satellite 'caught' the signal before the dish sent it; beats reordered. The channel's rule: never skip or misorder a causal step.

findings.title: QA round 1 failed, round 2 passed
findings.detail: Blocking: an empty sky at 5 s, a near-empty starfield at 70 s, white captions on the white dish. Fixed by reframing; round 2 passed.

findings.title: 3D dark stages fail the empty-frame gate
findings.detail: 51 then 16 of 85 stills were 'mostly empty background'; fixed with glowing motes and surface detail in every place (longform/backlog.json tech-long-3d-empty-frames).

findings.title: Render time
findings.detail: 426 s of 3D took about 7 hours on the cloud's software GL (05:18-12:04 UTC).

changes.title: Shipped L-20261123-21
changes.detail: Manifest on main (d46e435), mp4 on media/L-20261123-21 (90 MB parts). 426 s; liveliness median 10.4, no still stretches; peak -1.0 dB, mean -16.5 dB; thumbnails A 9/10 (picked), B 8, C 8.
